Fig. 1. Overview of the proposed semantic sampling framework. The input waveform x(t) is first mapped to multi-channel acoustic responses z(t) by a semantic feature filterbank HϑH . A constrained semantic observation matrix BϑB then combines these responses into observation channels u(t). The low-rate readout module S converts the observation responses into finite-dimensional samples y. A reconstruction network DϑD maps y back to the waveform domain through input projection, an encoder, a BiLSTM bottleneck, a decoder, and an output head.

Fig. 2. Waveform reconstruction results at different observation rates. Each row corresponds to one observation rate. The left column shows the reference waveform, and the following columns show the reconstructed waveforms and corresponding errors of Uniform-Sinc, AudioUNet, NU-Wave 2, AudioSR, and the proposed method.

Fig. 3. Spectrogram reconstruction results at different observation rates. Each row corresponds to one observation rate.
